title: Building digital trust: How John Deere governs AI, cybersecurity and digital risk
headline: John Deere's unified approach to AI and digital risk governance
summary: John Deere implements a unified enterprise framework that brings together cybersecurity, privacy, data governance, third-party risk, product security, and AI oversight. Company executives Jason Stanley and Brett Leighton discuss lessons learned from building this digital risk program over nearly a decade. They highlight strategies for managing AI governance, shadow AI, regulatory uncertainty, and intellectual property risk.
why_it_matters: Organisations can look to unified enterprise frameworks as a model for integrating AI oversight with existing cybersecurity, privacy, and third-party risk functions rather than managing AI in isolation.

quotes.text: Long before digital risk governance became a mainstream topic, John Deere was building a program designed to bring together cybersecurity, privacy, data governance, third-party risk, product security, and AI oversight under a unified framework.

In this in-depth conversation, Stanley and Leighton discuss how one of the world's most recognizable and technologically advanced manufacturers approaches digital trust; the lessons they've learned from nearly a decade of building an enterprise digital risk program; and how they're navigating everything from AI governance and shadow AI to regulatory uncertainty and intellectual property risk.

classification.significance_reason: An interview discussing enterprise risk management approaches in the manufacturing sector, offering general insights rather than specific regulatory or legal changes.
